operations.summary: What this API key can do
operations.description: The key's scopes, the plan tier, the rate limit, and which send-time safety checks apply to the account. Requires no scope: it exists so a client can plan its calls instead of discovering scopes through 403s.

Usage and plan limits in the same shape as Resend's GET /usage: emails in the last 24 hours and this month (with the reset time), contacts, segments, broadcasts this month, domains, and the rate limit. A null limit means no cap. Received mail does not count against the email limit, and prepaid credits are an extra field. On a team, the email quota and broadcast cap follow the team owner's plan and the domain limit the team's plan. Requires no scope.

Sending and deliverability totals for the account, plus a 30-day daily series. Pass days and/or domain to add a `window` object holding exact counts for that window and sending domain, aggregated in the database rather than sampled from the event log.

queryParams.name: days
queryParams.description: Window in days (1-90) for the `window` block. Present in the response only when days or domain is given.

queryParams.name: domain
queryParams.description: Restrict the `window` block to one sending domain, by name or id.

operations.description: Generate a new API key. The full key value is returned only once in the response. Store it securely.

fields.name: scopes
fields.description: Optional list of scopes to restrict the key. Available: email:send, email:read, domain:read, domain:write, contact:read, contact:write, form:read, form:write, webhook:read, webhook:write, apikey:manage. If omitted the key gets the default set (everything except apikey:manage). Listing, creating or revoking keys through the API requires apikey:manage.

operations.summary: Claim a domain held by another account
operations.description: Checks the claim TXT record and moves a never-verified domain from the account that holds it to the caller's team, with its verification reset and any mail the previous holder still had queued through it cancelled. POST /v1/domains answers 409 with code domain_claimable and the record when this applies. 422 claim_record_missing when the record is not visible, 503 dns_unavailable when the lookup itself failed. The previous holder is notified. Requires the domain:write scope; 20 checks per hour per team.

operations.summary: Get the claim record for a domain
operations.description: The TXT record a team publishes to prove DNS control before claiming a domain another account added but never verified. 404 when nobody holds the domain, 409 with code already_yours or verified_elsewhere when it cannot be claimed. Requires the domain:read scope.
Retrieve details for a single domain including its current verification status and DNS records.
Return all sending domains associated with the current account.

operations.summary: Turn inbound receiving on or off
operations.description: Enable or disable inbound email for a verified domain (paid plans). Returns the MX record to publish and the receiving status: disabled, pending, active or failed. Requires the domain:write scope.
Check whether the required DNS records have been configured correctly. If verification succeeds, the domain status changes to verified and it can be used for sending.
Cancel an email that has not been sent yet. Valid while the email is scheduled or queued; returns 409 once it has left for the provider. Requires the email:send scope.
Retrieve the current status and delivery events for a specific email by its ID.
List sent emails, newest first. Bodies are not included; fetch one with GET /v1/emails/{id}. Requires the email:read scope.

queryParams.description: The email id after which to retrieve more emails. Not returned in the list. Use either after or before, not both.

queryParams.name: before
queryParams.description: The email id before which to retrieve more emails. Not returned in the list. Use either after or before, not both.

queryParams.name: status
queryParams.description: Filter by current status, e.g. delivered, bounced, failed, scheduled.

operations.description: Queue a single email for delivery. The email is validated, queued, and sent asynchronously via the configured sending provider.

fields.name: attachments
fields.description: Up to 10 files, base64 encoded, 25 MB per message in total. A content_id makes the part inline: reference it from the HTML as cid:<content_id>.

fields.name: from
fields.description: Sender email address (must belong to a verified domain)

fields.name: html
fields.description: HTML body of the email. Include `{{unsubscribe_url}}` (or the Resend-compatible `{{{RESEND_UNSUBSCRIBE_URL}}}`) anywhere in the body and SMTPfast substitutes the per-recipient unsubscribe link at send time. The same URL is set on the RFC 8058 `List-Unsubscribe` header automatically.

fields.name: subject
fields.description: Email subject line

fields.name: text
fields.description: Plain text fallback body. Supports the same `{{unsubscribe_url}}` placeholder as the HTML body.

fields.name: to
fields.description: List of recipient email addresses

operations.description: Queue up to 100 emails in a single request. The body is a JSON array of email objects, each using the same shape as the single-send endpoint. Validation runs on every item before any are queued — a malformed item rejects the whole batch with 400. Suppressed recipients (to, cc and bcc) are dropped per row; a row left with no deliverable To recipient is recorded with status "failed".

operations.summary: Create a share link for a sent email
operations.description: Mint a public, expiring link to the rendered view of one sent email (the stored HTML or text body, in a sandboxed frame). Nothing is stored; the link stops working when it expires. Default lifetime 7 days, maximum 30. Requires the email:read scope.

fields.name: expires_in
fields.description: Lifetime in seconds (60 to 2592000)

operations.description: Change the send time of a scheduled email. Only scheduled_at can be changed; to change content, cancel and send again. Requires the email:send scope.

fields.name: scheduled_at
fields.description: New send time in ISO 8601. Must be in the future and within 30 days.

operations.description: Confirm pending signups without waiting for the link click, up to 200 per call; call again while `remaining` is above zero. Each one becomes a contact, fires contact.subscribed and gets the welcome email if enabled. Signups whose confirmation email bounced, was marked as spam or failed are left pending and counted in `skipped_undeliverable`. Signups submitted through Tor are left pending and counted in `skipped_tor`. Requires the form:write scope.

fields.name: q
fields.description: Only approve signups matching this search

operations.description: Confirm one pending signup without waiting for the link click. It becomes a contact, fires contact.subscribed and gets the welcome email if enabled. operations.description: The event log behind the dashboard Logs page: every lifecycle event of every sent email, newest first, with keyset pagination (after walks older, before walks newer, exclusive). queryParams.name: until

operations.description: Send a reply to a received message through the normal send pipeline (credits, suppression, safety checks, webhooks). The reply is threaded with In-Reply-To and References and linked to the received message. From defaults to the receiving address when its domain is verified for sending, otherwise to the same local part on the nearest verified parent domain with Reply-To set to the receiving address; pass from to pick another verified reply address. To defaults to the sender's Reply-To, then From. Requires the inbound:read and email:send scopes.

fields.description: One of the team's reply addresses for this message; see the dashboard detail's reply_from
